title_candidates: OpenAI is taking practical AI training to K-12 educators
summary: OpenAI Academy and the Walton Family Foundation are running hands-on AI Skills Jam sessions for K-12 educators across U.S. cities this summer.

primary_source.title: Helping K-12 educators build practical AI skills
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: OpenAI Academy is partnering with the Walton Family Foundation on AI Skills Jam sessions for K-12 educators.
The program is planned for more than 1,600 teachers, administrators, and district leaders in U.S. cities.
Sessions focus on hands-on classroom and school work, including lesson planning, communications, administrative tasks, and responsible adoption.
OpenAI points participants to OpenAI Academy as the free online platform for continuing after the in-person sessions.
The announcement cites Walton Family Foundation and Gallup research saying teachers who use AI weekly estimate saving 5.9 hours per week on average.

prerequisites: A school-safe AI policy or district guidance
An OpenAI Academy account if you want saved progress

steps.instruction: Check the OpenAI announcement for a nearby Skills Jam date or a district partner you recognize.
Open OpenAI Academy and search the K-12 Education area for educator-focused sessions.
Pick one low-risk task, such as drafting a parent email or turning existing notes into a lesson outline.
Remove student names, grades, health details, and private family information before using any AI tool.
Compare the AI draft against your district policy, then edit it before sending or sharing.

references.title: Helping K-12 educators build practical AI skills

risk_flags: Education use needs privacy discipline; article tells readers to remove student data and follow district policy.
